facts.claim: Prophet Muhammad died 632 CE
Battle of Yarmouk 636 CE, Byzantine defeat; Syria/Palestine under Arab control
Egypt conquered 639-642 CE
Battle of al-Qadisiyyah 636/637 CE
Battle of Nahavand 642 CE
Yazdegerd III, last Sasanian king, died 651 CE
Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed the Strait of Gibraltar 711 CE; Visigothic kingdom defeated
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh 711-712 CE, Raja Dahir defeated
Arab campaigns in Gujarat, Saurashtra, Kutch, Malwa in early 8th century
Gwalior inscription of Mihira Bhoja credits Nagabhata I with defeating a Mlechchha army, read as Arabs
Mihira Bhoja reigned c. 836-885 CE, capital Kannauj
Barah copper plate 836 CE and Daulatpura copper plate 843 CE of Bhoja
Father Ramabhadra's reign was troubled; Bhoja revived control of Gurjaratra
Tripartite Struggle: Pratiharas, Palas, Rashtrakutas over Kannauj
Arab merchant Sulaiman (851 CE): ruler of Juzr (Gurjara) had the finest cavalry among Indian princes
Sulaiman: the Gurjara king was the greatest foe/enemy of the Muslims (Islam)
facts.status: paraphrase in secondary sources; exact wording varies by translation

facts.claim: Pehowa (Prithudaka) inscription 882-83 CE: horse dealers' fair and donation to temples, reign of Bhoja
Adivaraha title on Bhoja's coins (boar = Varaha avatar of Vishnu)

Sulaiman's account (tr. Elliot & Dowson 1867, vol 1 p.4): the king of Jurz has numerous forces, no other Indian prince has so fine a cavalry; among the princes of India there is no greater foe of the Muhammadan faith
facts.status: verified (exact translated text shown on screen)

facts.claim: Gwalior prasasti of Bhoja, v.4: Nagabhata I defeated a Mlechchha army (Epigraphia Indica vol 18, p.101)

EI vol 18 p.103: shortly after 725 AD Arab invaders... Nagabhata gained successes over the Mlechchha forces; Nagabhata I established the greatness of his family by his triumphant success over the Arabs
Pehowa inscription (EI vol 1 p.184): horse-dealers at the horse-fair held at Pehoa (Prithudaka) imposed taxes for temples; Bhoja ruled in AD 882
Coin with Varaha on a Pratihara coin 850-900 CE
Gibraltar's name comes from Jabal Tariq (Tariq ibn Ziyad)
Banbhore (Sindh) is identified by many historians with Debal
Kailasa temple Ellora built under Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (8th century)
